items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Claude Jones sat down by me, and Walter Johnson, the drummer. He was right next to me, and the guys were all there.

ctx.x: out of there because you had no -- you know, if you fight back you're dead.

I remember another incident. We were in West Virginia in some little town called Richfield, West Virginia, and we played -- we went -- we got in this town and evidently it was something of a holiday, but we were hungry so we went in this -- we asked someone there, we saw one colored man in this town and we asked him where could we eat, and he said there's a restaurant across the street. He said, that's the only place in town that you can eat. He -- the only -- while he was there he was a bricklayer or something.…

So in walked about three white guys, and they didn't sit at the counter, because we were at the counter. They sat at a table right behind the counter, right,you know, not behind the counter but behind us. So we got our food and they asked the owner why did he serve these niggers before he served him -- served them, you know.
